diagnosis.summary: The nightly ingest for 2026-10-01 failed because order_items.csv now delivers quantity as strings like "1 units" instead of plain integers. The INTEGER cast fails on them. The only allow-listed parser is strip_currency, which doesn't handle this, so I found no safe automated fix and am escalating to the upstream app team. The change looks like a persistent format change, so a redelivery would probably return the same format.

root_cause.explanation: Upstream began sending order_items.quantity with a ' units' suffix (e.g. '1 units'). The 2026-09-30 file had plain integers. The ingest config is default, so the INTEGER cast raises a Conversion Error. Header and unit_price are unchanged. The suffix was seen in only 4 sampled rows, but the cast failure shows it is not isolated to those rows. The row count fell from 956 to 840, which I did not investigate.

evidence.claim: Ingest failed on casting quantity '1 units' to INT32 in raw.order_items
The 10-01 quantity values carry a ' units' suffix, 09-30 values are plain integers, and the header and unit_price are unchanged
No ingest parser or mapping is configured, so nothing handles the suffix
The only allow-listed parser is strip_currency ($ and ,). The runbooks say to escalate when no safe adaptation applies, and cover redelivery only for one-off bad files

alternatives_considered: set_column_parser strip_currency: does not strip ' units', so it would not fix the cast
request_upstream_redelivery: the format looks like a systematic upstream change, so the redelivery would likely have the same format
rerun_only: the same file would fail again
revert_model_change: failure is at ingest and no dbt model changed
apply_column_mapping or ignore_extra_columns: no columns were renamed or added
